title: Learning consequences target family
statement: Let $n$ be a natural number, let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\{−1,1\}$ be a Boolean function, let $t>0$ be a rational influence bound, and let $0<\varepsilon\leq 1/2$ be a rational learning parameter. The target family consists of the subsets of the influential coordinates of $f$ whose cardinalities are at most the learning consequences degree for $t$ and $\varepsilon$, with influence measured at the learning consequences threshold for those parameters.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
caveat: The snippet omits the definitions of influential coordinates, the threshold, and the degree, so their exact meanings cannot be fully rendered.
